issues.what: Every unsupervised fit (z-scoring, GMM, HMM, jump centroids and lambda, BOCPD standardisation, FFD d*) is frozen on the first IS half and then applied to its own bars, so the 35 model-derived columns are in-sample for the harness blocks that fall in 2021-10..2023-09 (blocks 0-4 fully, block 5 partly) and out-of-sample afterwards; the design's leakage control for regime-states says 'estimated on IS training-fold bars only, refit per fold'. Label-free, so no outcome can leak, and the caveat is stated, but not the block mapping nor that Judge 2's two-halves stability check for these columns compares an in-sample half with an out-of-sample half.
issues.evidence: Reproduced: fit window = IS & date in [2021-10-01, 2023-09-30] -> 182557 bars (1m) / 36514 bars (5m), 489 sessions, dates 2021-10-01..2023-09-29, last fit bar 182556 / 36513; IS has 1026 sessions so the fit half is 47.7% of IS; the truncation cut (bar 335934 / 67192, 2025-06-30 12:00) lies after the fit window, so trunc_diff cannot see the fit's own bars (the study says so).
issues.fix: State in FINDINGS/findings.json which harness blocks are in-sample for the frozen fit; the importance study should report the two-halves stability of gmm*/hmm*/jump*/bocpd*/ffd* as in-sample vs out-of-sample and discount the first half, or refit these features per training fold as the design specifies.

issues.what: d* for the FFD of log close is chosen on the fit window (0.2) while the design defines d* as the smallest d whose ADF passes on IS bars; on all IS bars d=0.2 fails the ADF at 5% and only 0.3 passes, so the shipped ffd_close_dstar is non-stationary by the design's own IS-wide rule. Disclosed as a caveat; label-free.
issues.evidence: Re-ran statsmodels adfuller(maxlag=2, autolag=None, regression='c') on 5minute log close FFD: d=0.2 fit window stat -5.246 (pass, crit -2.862), all IS stat -2.543 (fail); d=0.3 all IS -4.686 (pass); d=0.1 fails both. Matches the report's d_star_fit 0.2 / d_star_is 0.3.
issues.fix: Either ship a second column at the IS-wide d* (0.3), counted as one more candidate, or state in the README column row that the shipped series does not pass the ADF over all IS bars so the importance study treats it as a non-stationary candidate.
